sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1.3.1 (pp.4-6) gives Weining Neasu 11 retroflex consonants, vowel [ɤ], [i-y] contrast, four contrastive tones 55/33/21/13 with a minimal quadruplet, syllable template C(C)V(V)T; no mention of stress or accent anywhere in the book (grep stress/accent/prosod = 0 hits).

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) Languages. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington. 399 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Nesu (Weining) profile p.76: 'The Nesu has 46 initials, 8 vowels (7 monophthongs and 1 diphthong), 4 tones (/55/, /33/, /21/, and /13/) (cf. YYFC 1983)'; toneme Table 4.18 p.107. The word 'stress' does not occur in the dissertation.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Requests 2007-039 ([yig] renamed 'Nasu, Wusa') and 2007-038 ([ywu] 'Nasu, Wumeng'), submitted by J. Pelkey & D. Bradley.
sources.note: Nothing; denotation/naming only (Wusa = Guizhou-only Nasu variety).

Nothing on stress; its phonology section (rhotic vowels, 3 tones) is for a Yunnan Nasu variety, not Guizhou; used only for the Chen 1985 vernacular list (Wusa = Weining, Shuicheng, Hezhang, Nayong, Yiliang, Huize, Xuanwei).
